newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil, soymeal futures mostly down with soy.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil, soymeal futures mostly down with soy.

text.p: Moderate losses in CBOT soybean futures weighed on most soy product contracts at midsession Monday, floor traders said.
Heavy rains this weekend fell in dry areas of the U.S. Midwest. The moisture was said to alleviate overly dry conditions in central Illinois, Indiana and Ohio and benefit the crop, traders said.
Reports from Indian weather officials saying monsoonal rains were normal and promoting growth in oilseed crops there were also seen weighing on soyoil futures, traders said.
August soymeal was expected to find support from a sharp increase in the number of crushers taking downtime during the next two weeks, traders said.
Soyoil futures also garnered support from talk that this week's cool temperatures in the Midwest will cut into soyoil yields, traders said.
In early trade, commercials were small buyers in soymeal and were small sellers in soyoil, traders said.
At 1119 CDT, December soyoil was 0.18 cent lower at 22.45 cents a lb, with the others down 0.18 to 0.23. December meal was down $1.20 at $198.10 a ton, with the rest $0.20 higher to $1.80 lower.
